reason: The cited evidence shows that a dense glaze layer containing Al2O3 nanoparticles forms during high-temperature sliding in a different alloy (NiX) and reduces adhesive/oxidative wear, but it provides no support for the key premises about Al addition to CoCrFeNi, the low-temperature activation pre-treatment, or room-temperature oxide formation and performance.
premises: Adding ~5 at.% Al to CoCrFeNi will form a continuous, self-healing Al2O3 glaze during sliding
A low-temperature surface activation pre-treatment ensures a protective oxide is present at room temperature
The Al2O3 glaze reduces adhesive and oxidative wear across 25–800 °C
The adaptive oxide layer maintains low friction and wear rate over the full temperature range
